These two numbers are the checker's OWN readings on the real tree at land time (2026-09-19) — never hand-fitted. A reading above its baseline is RED; raising a baseline above the git-HEAD value is also RED (so 「调高基线」 cannot buy a pass). _axes.embeddedInterpreterLines: sum of code lines over tracked *.sh that are NOT in plugin/sh-census-exceptions.txt and contain an embedded interpreter (node with --experimental-strip-types/-e/.ts, python3, or jq) AT A COMMAND POSITION (comments / strings / heredoc bodies do not count).
_axes.duplicateCopies: count of non-symlink byte-identical same-basename pairs between experiments/**/scripts/ and plugin/scripts/ (includes .sh and .ts). Symlinked copies are counted separately as totals.symlinkedCopies and are NOT duplicates.

_reanchorLog.structuralNote: ⚠️ This re-anchor exposes a real weakness of the '只降不升' ratchet: any task that lands a NEW embedded-interpreter .sh raises the axis, and the only legal response is a committed re-anchor (which the shrink-guard permits once committed, since it compares worktree-vs-HEAD copies of this very file). So the guard reliably catches UNCOMMITTED (drifting) raises and forces committed raises to be visible/reviewable — but it CANNOT by itself prevent legitimate growth. Convergence therefore depends on Phase 4/5 actually removing the 1900-line capability-catalog.sh data table and the experiments/** mirrors, not on the ratchet alone.

_reanchorLog.why: This is the SHRINK the entry above predicted ('Convergence therefore depends on Phase 4/5 actually removing the 1900-line capability-catalog.sh data table'). Phase 4 moved the 10 declare -A declaration tables out of plugin/scripts/capability-catalog.sh into capability-catalog-declarations.json, read by a new TypeScript renderer; the .sh is now a thin exec wrapper. Lowering a baseline is the intended direction (this file's _note: 'needs no ceremony, but the file change must still be committed') — it is committed here, and both numbers are again the checker's OWN reading on the tree, never hand-fitted.

_reanchorLog.structuralNote: ↘ This is the first DECREASE on this axis, and it validates the Phase 4 direction: the two ratchet axes were chosen on the premise that the shell corpus is the thing to shrink, and moving DATA out of a shell file into a data file is a real, mechanical way to do it (the hazard removed was not line count but shell EVALUATION of shell-quoted data). Note what did NOT move: the axis counts effective lines of embedded-interpreter .sh, so a thin wrapper around a TS renderer still counts — 'make it thin' is rewarded, 'make it JS' is not what this axis measures.
